commands.author: yetval

target.title: gateway: fs.listDir node pairing can be approved without operator.admin
target.body:
## Summary
A caller with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write`, but without `operator.admin`, can approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`. The same command is explicitly admin-gated when it is invoked, so the pairing trust decision is weaker than the command's execution boundary.

## Environment
- Commit: a674ce5e0d1ab0774546086fa7b2730516eca176 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: Gateway node pairing authorization and node-host filesystem directory browsing

## Steps to reproduce
1. Register a pending node pairing request whose declared commands are `["fs.listDir"]`.
2. Call `node.pair.approve` with an operator session containing `operator.pairing` and `operator.write`, but not `operator.admin`.
3. Observe that the pairing is accepted and persists `fs.listDir` on the node surface.

## Expected
Approving a node surface that declares `fs.listDir` should require `operator.admin`, matching the existing invoke-time authorization for that command.

## Actual
The approval-scope resolver classifies `fs.listDir` as a generic non-exec command and requires only `operator.pairing` plus `operator.write`. The accepted surface is then persisted by the real pairing approval path.

## Root cause
`src/infra/node-pairing-authz.ts:11` defines the commands that need admin approval:

```ts
const ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS = [...NODE_SYSTEM_RUN_COMMANDS, NODE_BROWSER_PROXY_COMMAND];
```

`fs.listDir` was added in #105114 and is included in `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS` in `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts:115`, but it was never added to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`. `approveNodePairing` calls `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` before it persists the node surface, so every `node.pair.approve` path uses the weaker mapping.

## Sibling surfaces
#104491 fixed the same approval-versus-invocation scope mismatch for `browser.proxy` by adding that command to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`. This report concerns the separate `fs.listDir` command introduced later in #105114. The command is live: it is advertised by the node command policy, accepted by the node host runtime, and dispatched by the `fs.listDir` gateway handler. This is not an unreachable or dead declaration.
